wa_6_main_cliff.blurb: Main Cliff is the tallest wall in the Farside and Dropzone zone along Highway 14 in the Columbia Gorge, and it holds the area's best-regarded lines. Nearly every route here is trad, with a single sport line, and the area as a whole has been kept deliberately light on bolts. Difficulty runs from 5.8 up to the low 5.12s, though the bulk of the climbs sit in the 5.10 range, so it suits climbers who already lead on gear. A few lines are runout. The wall is reached by either of two trails descending from the roadside pullouts.
wa_6_main_cliff.parking_note: Leave the car in the gravel pullouts on the south side of Highway 14, near mile 24. The larger pullout sits at the top of the hill, with a smaller one just west of it. Avoid the slow-vehicle ramp.

wa_big_butte_south_face.blurb: The south face is the biggest of Big Butte's three walls in the Okanogan country, with a mix of trad, sport and mixed lines. It is a friendly spot for newer leaders: the grades run from about 5.2 to 5.8, and the far-right bolted lines are gentle and good for practicing gear placements with a bolt nearby. The wall faces south and takes sun all day, and the flat grassy ground at its foot works well for groups and families. Bolts on the easiest routes can feel widely spaced for a very first lead.

wa_busted_boulder.blurb: Busted Boulder is one of the main stops within the Forestland Boulders, in the Icicle Creek zone outside Leavenworth. It holds thirteen problems and nothing else but bouldering. The spread leans hard: a single easy problem, a few around V4, then a solid block between V6 and V8, with a couple of problems beyond that. Its most-repeated lines are high-grade classics on the biggest block, which sits out in the open once you reach the clearing. A short walk from the parking area gets you there, and the clearing is shared with many other boulders.
wa_busted_boulder.approach: From the Forestland parking area, follow the trail into the woods until it opens into a clearing full of boulders. Busted Boulder is the largest block straight ahead.

wa_hueco_crimper_boulder.blurb: This roadside boulder in Tumwater Canyon near Leavenworth sits right on a river beach and is part of the Pitless Avocado zone. Thirteen problems share it, ranging from easy V2s up to V10, with a handful in each band, so there is something for almost any boulderer. The line that gives the boulder its name is the best known problem here. Expect the base to be covered by water for 2 to 3 feet in spring, so it is best visited once the river drops.

wa_hummel_s_landing.blurb: Hummel's Landing is a small practice crag overlooking Hummel's Cove, one of the sub-areas of McLellan Rocks in Riverside State Park near Nine Mile Falls. The thirteen routes are mostly short trad lines with a few sport routes, and most fall between 5.4 and 5.7, with one harder line near 5.10. That makes it a gentle place to learn gear placements and to get new partners started. The top of the cliff gives plenty of room to build anchors, and the lines can be reached from above.

wa_main_corridor.blurb: Main Corridor is the central inner passage of Horsethief Butte in south-central Washington, with its routes laid out from left to right along the south wall. Most of the climbing is trad, with a pair of short boulder problems in the easy V1 to V2 range and a single top-rope line around 5.10. The traditional lines are mostly low grade, in the 5.3 to 5.8 range, so it is a handy spot for beginners and for easy gear leads. Most climbs are rated two stars.

wa_mirabeau_park.blurb: Mirabeau Park is a small crag in a city park, right in the heart of Spokane Valley, and is nearly all sport climbing, with one trad line. Textured holds make the climbing better than its size suggests. Routes run from about 5.7 to 5.12, with a good cluster of 5.10s and several 5.11s and 5.12s, so it suits intermediate and stronger sport climbers. Many of the bolted lines can be top-roped, and the setting is easy for kids. It is a quick after-work option rather than a destination.
